Pattern: danh từ đếm được; a + media conglomerate + owns
Examples: One media conglomerate owns the paper and the channel. | Media conglomerates sell the advertising as a package.

Pattern: danh từ đếm được; a + press baron + dictates
Examples: The press baron dictated the editorial line by telephone. | Press barons outlasted most of the politicians they attacked.

Definition: sự độc lập về biên tập
Pattern: danh từ không đếm được; guarantee/lose + editorial independence
Examples: Editorial independence was guaranteed in writing and ignored. | Without editorial independence a newsroom is a press office.

Pattern: danh từ đếm được; breach/sign up to + a code of practice
Examples: The code of practice forbids payment to witnesses. | They breached the code of practice on two counts.

Pattern: danh từ không đếm được; assert/breach + the right to privacy
Examples: The court weighed the right to privacy against the public interest. | Her right to privacy ended at the hospital door, they argued.

Pattern: hype + N; thường bị động
Examples: The launch was hyped for a month. | They hyped a routine appointment into a crisis.

Pattern: disclose + N + to + sb; thường bị động
Examples: The report was disclosed to two papers. | Nobody disclosed the payments until the audit.

Definition: cung cấp thông tin (cho báo chí)
Pattern: brief + sb + on/about + N
Examples: Advisers briefed four papers that evening. | She briefed the press before telling her own department.

Definition: đăng nổi bật trên trang nhất
Pattern: splash + N + across/on + N
Examples: They splashed the photograph across the front page. | The story was splashed on every tabloid.

Pattern: corroborate + N; thường bị động
Examples: The footage could not be corroborated. | Two departments corroborated the figure.

Pattern: attribute + N + to + sb; thường bị động
Examples: The quote was attributed to an unnamed official. | They attributed the claim to a single document.

Pattern: circulate; circulate among + N
Examples: The recording circulated for a week before anyone checked it. | Rumours circulated among staff before the announcement.

Pattern: amplify + N; thường bị động
Examples: The claim was amplified by nine large accounts. | Repeating a lie to correct it amplifies it.

Pattern: debunk + N; thường bị động
Examples: The theory was debunked in the same week. | They debunked the figure line by line.

Pattern: an in-depth + N (report, interview)
Examples: An in-depth report ran across three pages. | In-depth interviews take a day to prepare.

Pattern: a hard-hitting + N (documentary, editorial)
Examples: A hard-hitting documentary forced the resignation. | The editorial was hard-hitting and carefully lawyered.

Pattern: a one-sided + N (account, debate)
Examples: The coverage was one-sided for a fortnight. | A one-sided account is not the same as a lie.

Pattern: inflammatory + N (language, headline)
Examples: Inflammatory language on the front page preceded the violence. | The regulator called the headline inflammatory.

Pattern: intrusive + N (coverage, photography)
Examples: Intrusive coverage followed the family to the funeral. | The photography was intrusive by any standard.

Pattern: a misleading + N (headline, figure)
Examples: The headline was accurate and thoroughly misleading. | Two misleading graphs were withdrawn.

Pattern: a widely read + N (column, blog)
Examples: The column is widely read inside government. | A widely read blog broke the story first.

Pattern: an award-winning + N (series, reporter)
Examples: An award-winning series was cancelled anyway. | Their award-winning reporter left for a charity.

Pattern: a pre-recorded + N (interview, segment)
Examples: The interview was pre-recorded and heavily cut. | A pre-recorded message answered every question.

Pattern: a prime-time + N (slot, audience)
Examples: The debate was given a prime-time slot. | A prime-time audience sees nine advertisements an hour.

Definition: được bán lại cho nhiều nơi đăng
Pattern: a syndicated + N (column, feature)
Examples: The syndicated column appears in forty papers. | Syndicated features replaced local writing.

Pattern: a defamatory + N (claim, article)
Examples: Two sentences were found to be defamatory. | They removed the defamatory paragraph and kept the rest.

Pattern: put out + N hoặc put + N + out; tách được
Examples: The department put out a statement at midnight. | They put a correction out on page nineteen.

Pattern: run with + N; không tách được
Examples: Two papers ran with the unverified version. | They ran with the headline and apologised later.

Pattern: dig up + N hoặc dig + N + up; tách được
Examples: Reporters dug up a letter from 1994. | They dug his old interviews up within hours.

Definition: tiếp tục theo dõi, làm rõ
Pattern: follow up + N hoặc follow + N + up; tách được
Examples: Nobody followed up the first complaint. | She followed the lead up for three months.

Pattern: call out + N hoặc call + N + out; tách được
Examples: Readers called out the error within minutes. | She called the broadcaster out on air.

Definition: giữ nguyên quan điểm đã nêu
Pattern: stand by + N; không tách được
Examples: The editor stood by the story for a year. | They stood by every word of the headline.

Pattern: rake up + N hoặc rake + N + up; tách được
Examples: The piece raked up a case from his twenties. | They raked the old dispute up again.

Pattern: hold back + N hoặc hold + N + back; tách được
Examples: The paper held back the name for legal reasons. | They held the pictures back until the trial ended.

Pattern: spread like wildfire
Examples: The clip spread like wildfire before anyone checked the date. | The rumour spread like wildfire through the whole estate.

Pattern: be/on + a slow news day
Examples: The story ran because it was a slow news day. | On a slow news day a planning notice becomes a scandal.

Pattern: speak/say sth + off the cuff
Examples: The remark was off the cuff and cost him the post. | She answered off the cuff and was quoted for weeks.

Pattern: read between the lines
Examples: Read between the lines and the resignation was already agreed. | Readers were left to read between the lines.

Pattern: a campaign of + mud-slinging
Examples: The contest descended into mud-slinging. | Mud-slinging between the two camps filled the airtime.

Pattern: break the news + about/of + N
Examples: A weekly paper broke the news of the closure. | They broke the news an hour before the official statement.

Pattern: be/put sth + in the public domain
Examples: The documents were already in the public domain. | Putting the figures in the public domain ended the argument.
